title: Cárdenas and the goals of the Mexican Revolution
stem: Paper 3 (History of the Americas) essay practice. Plan for about 50 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: To what extent did the presidency of Lázaro Cárdenas (1934–1940) fulfil the aims of the 1917 Constitution?
markscheme: Introduction identifying the Constitution's key aims (Articles 3, 27, 123, 130) and a clear thesis
Land (Article 27): large-scale redistribution as ejidos, far more than previous presidents
Limitations of land reform: poor credit and productivity on many ejidos; private estates survived in some regions
Subsoil rights (Article 27): oil expropriation, 18 March 1938, and creation of PEMEX
Labour (Article 123): support for strikes and the CTM; but workers incorporated into the party
Education (Article 3): expansion of rural and 'socialist' education, and its controversy
Church (Article 130): Cárdenas eased conflict with the Church compared with Calles and the Cristero War
Political change: exile of Calles (1936), PRM sectors (1938) building a corporatist one-party system rather than democracy
Historiography: Cárdenas as fulfilment of the revolution versus revisionist view of state-building and control
Conclusion with a judgement on the extent
parts.notes: Real Paper 3 essays are marked out of 15; this practice version uses a 10-point checklist. Use precise dates and figures.
